column1: Now let’s see what this production function says about economic growth. As before, we assume a fraction s of income is saved and invested. We therefore describe capital accumulation with an equation similar to those we used previously: DK 5 sY  K. This equation states that the change in the capital stock (DK ) equals investment (sY ) minus depreciation (K ). Combining this equation with the Y 5 AK production function, we obtain, after a bit of manipulation, DY/Y 5 DK/K 5 sA  . This equation shows what determines the growth rate of output DY/Y. Notice that, as long as sA  , the economy’s income grows forever, even without the assumption of exogenous technological progress.
